chunks.text:
What is an online student advocate?

An advocate supports students with navigation, resources, and overall success. Your advocate partners with academic advisors across the university to assist with planning an executing your degree plan.

What kind of support will I receive as an Online+ student?

From application to graduation, you’ll have personalized support (opnes in new tab), including:

Link for "personalized support (opnes in new tab)": https://www.depts.ttu.edu/online/advocates/

Step 1: Enrollment Service Specialists to guide you through admissions

Step 2: Online Student Advocates for academic and financial aid assistance

Step 3: Career counseling and job placement resources

If I need to withdraw from a course that is not required, will that count towards my withdraw amounts that I am allowed, even if it was told that I needed it and then later told that it is not required?

You should always check in with your Online Student Advocate regarding any course withdrawals to understand the implications fully. Additionally, it's essential to review the Academic and Financial Calendars to determine any consequences of withdrawing. If you feel that you were recommended a course that you did not need, please let your Online Student Advocate know immediately so they can explore options to support you.

When it comes to withdrawals, they can count towards limits set by your institution, so discussing this specific situation with your Online Student Advocate will provide clarity on how it affects your allowed withdraw amounts.

Graduate+ students do not have a drop limit.

Remember, before making any decisions, consider discussing the financial consequences of withdrawing with your financial aid advisor.

Accepted? Work with Your Online Student Advocate

Once admitted, you’ll be paired with an Online Student Advocate (OSA) who will help you register for classes and plan your degree path.

How we help:

Step 1: Review your degree plan and transfer credits

Step 2: Help with course registration

Step 3: Answer questions about online student success

Answer

Need Help Registering for Classes? Find Your Online Student Advocate:

Table of Contents

Can my Online Student Advocate Register me for classes?

Step 1: Your Online Student Advocate (OSA) provides support, guidance, and resources to help you succeed, but they do not directly register you for classes.

Step 2: Registration for classes must be completed by the student through Raiderlink.

Step 3: Your OSA can assist you with course planning, answer questions about the registration process, and help resolve any issues you encounter.

Step 2: For step-by-step instructions on how to register, refer to Raiderlink or contact your OSA for support.

Please note: Students must complete the Financial Responsibility Agreement via Raiderlink for an Online Student Advocate to assist with the registration process.

Why would I be placed on probation if I have never withdrawn from a course and my GPA is higher than 2.0?

Probation status can depend on academic program factors beyond just withdrawing from courses or maintaining a GPA above 2.0. Each institution may have specific policies related to academic probation that consider factors such as overall academic performance, course completion rate, or adherence to university guidelines. It would be beneficial to contact your Online Student Advocate or consult the academic policies laid out by Texas Tech University for clarification on your specific situation regarding probation. For any personalized inquiries, you can reach out to Texas Tech Online+ at online@ttu.edu or call 1-806-515-4465.

Graduate+ students, please note that the Graduate School requires a Grade Point Average (GPA) of 3.0 or above.

Would Online+ be a good fit for someone that did not finish high school but got their GED?

Online+ may be an option if you have obtained a GED. We require an official high school transcript for any high school coursework completed before obtaining your GED. Official transcripts must be sent directly from the high school to Texas Tech University to Admissions.Transcripts@ttu.edu if sent electronically. If sent from the high school by mail, it must be in the original sealed envelope and sent directly to TTUO Admissions, 4201 State Hwy 161 Suite 250, Irving, TX 75038. *We cannot accept transcripts that are emailed or uploaded by students. Transcripts may take several business days to be downloaded, received, and processed by Texas Tech University. GED scores can be emailed to the student’s Enrollment Service Specialist for the application.

Online+ is designed to remove barriers for working adults and nontraditional students by combining flexibility with high-touch support and predictable scheduling.

The Bachelor of Applied Arts and Sciences (BAAS) in Emergency Management is a fully online completer program designed for students who have earned an Associate of Applied Science (AAS) in emergency management, fire science or a related field from an accredited community college.

Emergency management is a vital and rapidly evolving profession focused on safeguarding communities against natural, technological and human-made hazards. Texas Tech University has designed this curriculum to provide graduates with the advanced knowledge and skills needed to succeed in this demanding field. This degree builds on foundational knowledge gained in associate programs, combined with professional experience, to deliver a strong upper-level core based on all-hazards principles.

Students study hazard identification and risk assessment, emergency planning and preparedness, incident command, disaster recovery, continuity planning, mitigation strategies, resilience building, leadership, crisis communication, and policy, legal and ethical issues. Courses are delivered entirely online in an asynchronous 8-week format.

The program emphasizes real-world application through case studies, simulations, peer discussions and a capstone project. Students build on their professional experience while strengthening skills in interagency coordination, ethical decision-making and policy development. They also learn from faculty with extensive industry experience and connect with peers to build valuable professional networks.

Prepare for Texas school counselor certification with Texas Tech’s online Master of Education in School Counseling. This 48-credit-hour graduate program integrates counseling theory, ethical practice, diversity, assessment and supervised practicum experience in K–12 settings.

Texas Tech University’s Online Master of Education in School Counseling is a 48-credit-hour graduate program designed to prepare candidates for Texas school counselor certification. The curriculum integrates counseling theory, ethical and legal foundations, diversity, career development, assessment, crisis intervention, and child and adolescent counseling. Students build competencies in individual and group counseling, family systems, addiction awareness and culturally responsive practice. **VA Benefits for Texas Tech University Online+ Students**

Texas Tech University Online+ students may be eligible to use VA education benefits, including the GI Bill®, for their online degree programs. Here’s what you need to know:

**Key Points:**
- Texas Tech Online+ programs are accredited and eligible for VA education benefits.
- You must be admitted to an eligible degree program to use VA benefits.
- The VA may have specific requirements for online coursework and enrollment status.

**How to Use VA Benefits at TTU Online+:**
1. **Apply for Admission:**  
   - Complete your application to an eligible Texas Tech Online+ program.

2. **Apply for VA Benefits:**  
   - Visit the VA website to apply for education benefits: VA Education Benefits
   - Obtain your Certificate of Eligibility (COE) from the VA.

3. **Submit Documentation to Texas Tech:**  
   - Provide your COE and any required forms to the Texas Tech Military & Veterans Programs (MVP) office.

4. **Register for Courses:**  
   - Enroll in courses that apply toward your degree plan.

5. **Certification:**  
   - The MVP office will certify your enrollment to the VA each term.

**Support Contacts:**
- **Texas Tech Military & Veterans Programs (MVP):**
  - Website: [MVP Contact Us](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/mvp/contact_us.php)
  - Email: mvp@ttu.edu
  - Phone: 806-742-6877

**Next Step:**  
Contact the MVP office for personalized guidance on using your VA benefits with Texas Tech Online+.

If you need help with the application or enrollment process, you can also reach TTU Online+ at 1-844-691-0494 or online@ttu.edu.

The Advanced School Counseling Certificate is designed for professionals who have already earned a master’s degree in counseling and are seeking to become certified school counselors in Texas. This 12-hour graduate certificate is delivered 100% online through asynchronous coursework and provides the specialized preparation required for Texas School Counselor certification.

The curriculum develops the knowledge and skills necessary to support the academic, career, personal, and social development of K–12 students. Students learn to design, implement, and evaluate comprehensive school counseling programs; collaborate with educators, families, and community partners; advocate for equitable student outcomes; and provide developmentally appropriate counseling services within school settings.

The certificate includes the coursework and supervised practicum required by the Texas Education Agency (TEA) for certification. Candidates complete a 160-hour supervised practicum in an approved Texas K–12 school setting under the supervision of a qualified school counselor and in accordance with Texas Tech University’s Educator Preparation Program (EPP) requirements.

This certificate is intended for individuals who already hold a master’s degree in counseling and wish to expand their professional practice into the K–12 educational setting without completing an additional master’s degree.

Completion of the certificate satisfies the educational and practicum requirements for Texas School Counselor certification through Texas Tech University’s approved Educator Preparation Program. Candidates must also meet all applicable Texas Education Agency certification requirements, including passing the required certification examination and any additional state requirements in effect at the time of application for certification.

Digital badge. An online record that shows you finished a microcredential. You earn one for each course.

Prior learning credit. Credit for work or life experience, not for a college class. An advisor helps you build a prior learning portfolio. This program can award up to 9 credit hours this way. Together with the microcredentials, that can be up to 21 credit hours before you pay to convert them.

Flat program fee. One set price, not a charge for each credit hour, to turn completed microcredentials and prior learning into official credit toward your degree. The microcredential classes themselves are free. This fee is what converts that work, and eligible prior learning, into degree credit.

Concentration. A focused set of courses in one subject. In the Bachelor of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies, you choose three.

Non-traditional learner. An adult returning to college, often while working, rather than a recent high-school graduate attending full time. This program is built for you.

What is considered "full-time" for 8-week courses?

Full-time status is 6 hours each 8-week term.

How many courses should I take per term?

Most students take 1–2 courses per 8-week term depending on their schedule. 2 courses per term are required to be considered “full-time” enrolled.

Graduate Enrollment Status (8-Week Model)

Step 1: Full-time: 6 credit hours

Step 2: Half-time: 3–5 credit hours

Step 3: Less than half-time: 1–2 credit hours

How does financial aid work in 8-week terms?

Financial aid eligibility is based on enrollment status within the academic period.

Enrollment Status for Financial Aid:

Step 1: Full-time: 6 credit hours

Step 2: Half-time: 3–5 credit hours

Step 3: Less than half-time: 1–2 credit hours

Aid eligibility and disbursement may vary depending on enrollment level. Students should be referred to the Financial Aid Office for individualized guidance.

Comprehensive Evaluation

All TTU graduate students MUST complete a comprehensive evaluation in order to graduate. There are four (4) different options for students in the CS Dept. to complete this.

Step 1: Master's Thesis

Step 2: Students must publicly defend their completed thesis to satisfy this requirement. Six (6) hours of CS 6000 - Master's thesis AND CS faculty approval are required.

Step 3: Master's Project

Step 4: Students will complete an oral examination wherein they present publicly on project results. Requires three (3) credit hours of CS 6001 - Master's Project AND CS faculty approval.

Step 5: Industry Career Certificate through Coursera

Step 8: Students can participate in an approved internship/CPT (see grad advisor). The internship/CPT requires co-enrollment in CS 5000 - Practicum in Computer Science.

The CS Dept. no longer offers an exam option or a report option.

Am I eligible for Amazon Career Choice?

Every student has unique obligations and responsibilities that have an impact on when and where they can engage in learning, but that shouldn't hold them back from earning a graduate degree. That's why you can attend our program as a full-time or part-time student and why most of the curriculum is offered with an asynchronous modality. Students in our online MSW program can mold study time to whatever schedule works best for them, from first thing in the morning all the way to the wee hours of nightime. Whatever time it is, your class materials will be waiting for you. On the other hand, we know from experience that most students want some face-to-face time to get to know their professors and peers, as well as to ask questions and get help. In the TTU Online MSW program, you'll have the option to drop-in during professors' real-time office hours and attend real-time meet-ups at least a few times each semester.

Comprehensive Evaluation/Comprehensive Examination

All TTU graduate students MUST complete a comprehensive evaluation in order to graduate. There are four (4) different options for students in the CS Dept. to complete this:

Two Distinct Program Admission Tracks

Online Advanced Admission:

$10K Degree Completion Program. Texas Tech's pathway for adults who already have college credit and want to finish a bachelor's degree. Applicable credit hours. College credit that counts toward this degree, not every credit you have earned. Core curriculum (core courses). The general-education courses you need before you can finish a bachelor's degree. This program expects those courses to be complete before you start.

Asynchronous. Coursework you complete on your own schedule. It is not a live class at a set time. After the microcredentials, the rest of the degree is taught this way.
